Then Zengi spoke with the nobles and said:
"You know what happened to al-Mustarshid on account of the dissension of his nobles,
when neither he nor they found good.
Now therefore, if your intention is steadfast
and you are prepared with alacrity to do battle with Sultan Mas'ud,
tell me, that I may know (or: that I may meet him).
And if not,
why are you attacking and being plundered and broken? Depart, each one to his place,
while your possessions are still preserved for you."
And when the mouth of all of them was stopped and they did not answer,
but were only looking at one another,
Zengi knew that they were deceitful,
and he told the Caliph.
And they all arose again and entered the city,
and pitched their tents inside the wall.
Then Zengi immediately left and went to Mosul.
And when the Caliph saw that he had departed,
neither was he able to hold out,
but he abandoned everything and fled, he too, with Zengi to Mosul.
Then Sultan Mas'ud entered Baghdad,
and dealt kindly with the people of Baghdad,
and would not allow even one house to be plundered.
And he gathered all the nobles,
and brought out and showed them the handwriting of the Caliph Rashid,
stipulating that on whatever day he should assemble forces
and go out to engage even an emir from the emirs of Sultan Mas'ud,
he would be deposed from the caliphate.
And when the witnesses who had their handwritings on it (the document) were brought forward,
and their testimonies were confirmed,
they legally deposed Rashid from the caliphate.
And they also brought other charges against him:
that he had gone in unto maidservants
with whom his father had cohabited,
and that he drank wine,
and neglected the prayers,
and played with the ball (polo),
and that he acted unjustly and oppressively,
and shed innocent blood.
Al-Muqtafi, his uncle, the son of al-Mustazhir,
twenty-four years and two months.
When Rashid was deposed,
the Sultan summoned Sharaf al-Din Zayni the vizier,
and entrusted to him the choice of who should succeed.
And he chose the uncle of him who had been deposed,
because he was his son-in-law, his daughter's husband.

and brought al-Muqtafi,
